item.description: China has launched a rare air force support and training centre in Laos, the Ministry of Defence announced on Tuesday. The China-Laos Joint Support and Training Centre and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy are now in operation at the Ban Keun Airport, aiming to help the Laotian Air Force train its pilots, the ministry said in a statement. item.description: The US Navy has set up a dedicated command to turn its growing array of aerial, surface and underwater drones into an integrated fighting force – a capability US commanders have linked to disrupting a PLA attack on Taiwan. The Robotic and Autonomous Systems Warfighting Development Centre, formally established on September 24 in Virginia, will develop doctrine and tactics for unmanned systems, train sailors to use them, and test whether they can keep operating under realistic conditions. item.title: SCMP: What trap? US-China relations show conflict is far from inevitable
item.description: For a decade, foreign policy circles have treated war between the United States and China as something close to destiny. The theory has a fancy, fashionable name borrowed from ancient Greece: the “Thucydides Trap” – the idea that a rising power and an established one are fated to collide, the way two articulated lorries merging into a single lane rarely ends well. The term is widely used in commentaries on US-China relations. Frictions get written off as “inevitable” regardless of what…

item.title: CGTN (Chinese state media): The Mind-Blowing Mirror Power Plant in China's Desert
item.description: Historically Dunhuang, on the northeastern edge of the Taklimakan Desert, was a Han Dynasty commandery and a hub on the Silk Road. Today, it's the location of China's first 100-megawatt molten-salt tower solar thermal plant. With more than 12,000 heliostats, it stores heat and generates power around the clock, despite the constant menace of sandstorms.

item.title: CGTN (Chinese state media): Sichuan's Largest Grotto Complex
item.description: The first carvings at the Thousand-Buddha Cliff in Guangyuan, on the east bank of the Jialing River, date from the late Northern Wei Dynasty (386–534 AD). The site entered its golden age during the Tang Dynasty (618–907). Today comprising more than 7,900 statues, it is the largest grotto complex in Sichuan Province.

item.description: For centuries, shadow puppetry has lived on white screens in village theaters — a craft where every cut and every performance takes time. But today, a team from Tsinghua University's Academy of Arts & Design is giving it a new stage, powered by artificial intelligence.
